feeds.title: Tin Can Knits
feeds.description: Here Tin Can Knits we love all things knitting and design. We love lace, cables, textures, garments, accessories, sizes for all, and we don't really enjoy seaming. Tin Can Knits is the collaboration of two Canadian designers; Alexa Ludeman and Emily Wessel. With accessible and clearly written patterns, beautiful photography and heartfelt stories, and we aim to share our love of knitting, and inspire you to do the same!

feeds.title: Yarn Harlot
feeds.description: A writer, knitter, blogger Steph Pearl-McPhee goes on (and on) about Knitting. Sharing knitting, yarn and her lumpy over spun spinning escapades.

feeds.title: SweetGeorgia Yarns Blog
feeds.description: Founded in 2005 by Felicia Lo, SweetGeorgia Yarns is an artisan yarn company that is passionate about bringing you stunningly saturated colors, luxurious natural fibers, and yarns of the highest quality. It is a yarn and fiber arts company that creates luxury hand-dyed yarn, fiber, patterns, goods, and education for a global community to bring joy.

feeds.title: The Blue Brick
feeds.description: Each skein of Blue Brick yarn is inspired by a photograph taken by us. They are individually hand-painted in a pet-friendly, smoke-free home.

feeds.title: Paper Tiger
feeds.description: I share my current and future knitting projects and patterns as well as snippets of my life here. My name is Dianna and I'm a serial expat, living in central Norway.

feeds.title: Sweet Paprika Designs - Hand-dyed yarn, knitting patterns, kits
feeds.description: Based in Montreal, Canada, here at Sweet Paprika we create luxurious artisan hand-dyed yarns, knitting and crochet patterns and kits, and run yarn clubs.

feeds.title: Needles in the Hay
feeds.description: swing the yarn around the needle, find the Needles in the Hay! We work hard to bring you the best selection of high quality yarns at a variety of price points and we search high and low to make sure you're getting the best products at the best value.

feeds.title: Knitatude
feeds.description: I'm a Chantal Miyagishima! The philosophy behind Knitatude is knitting with attitude. Knitting is my jam, my love, and my obsession. I started small with making my own items, then grew when friends and family loved my stuff. I love all things knit, big cozy sweaters, and feeling as comfy in my skin as I possibly can - which includes swearing (a lot!).

feeds.title: Baaad Anna's Yarn Store
feeds.description: Baaad Anna's provides affordable, diverse, and eco-friendly yarn, knitting supplies and classes. We strive to create a community space for diverse crafters, parents, artists and non-conformist knitters in the East Van Neighbourhood.

feeds.title: A Really Good Yarn by Julie
feeds.description: Patterns with the yarn! I started knitting at 4 years old. By the time I was 8 my mind was made up that I would own a yarn store. That dream came true at 19-now I'm into the 27th year of that dream.

feeds.title: Yarn Spinner
feeds.description: Joanne Seiff enjoys making things from scratch; she's been knitting since she was four or five and spinning since she was 12. Joanne is a writer, knitwear designer and educator.

feeds.title: Tanis Fiber Arts
feeds.description: TFA is a home-based, independent yarn company created by Tanis Lavallee. Where you'll find up-to-the-minute updates on all the TFA goings on! We specialize in gorgeous tonals & fantastic yardage. We are always working on developing new patterns and are experimenting with new yarn bases all the time!

feeds.title: The Knitting Needle and the Damage Done
feeds.description: On my blog, I critique and ridicule selected patterns from the most recent issues of all the major knitting magazines.

feeds.title: Espace Tricot Blog
feeds.description: As much a gathering place as a retail space, Espace Tricot's inspiring atmosphere caters to fiber lovers of all ages and skill levels, attracting a loyal clientele.

feeds.title: The Knit Café
feeds.description: We love yarn! So much so we are compelled to compose knitting patterns that take advantage of all of our yarns best qualities. We also love teaching and sharing the love of crafting! We host lots of classes here at the cafe and are always available to trouble shoot knit-trials, large and small.

feeds.title: Quilt, Knit, Run, Sew
feeds.description: Living in Eastern Canada, I have 6 grandchildren. I can't imagine life without them. I share my love for Quilting, Sewing, Running, Knitting, Crazy Quilting.

feeds.title: Wolf & Faun Knits: Artisan Fibre Arts Tools and Knitting Patterns
feeds.description: A unique online Canadian knitting shop offering artisan made notions and tools for knitters and other fibre artists. Featuring knit designs by Nat Raedwulf

feeds.title: Chris Knits in Niagara
feeds.description: I golf, knit, sew, felt and work in the Beautiful Niagara Region, the banana belt of Canada. I work in the optical field, and love to combine fashion and great vision in eyewear. I knit, and sew, and felt, most of the other hours of the day. My felted goods are available for purchase on Etsy or at Pamela's in Jordan Village.

feeds.title: Robin Hunter Designs - How to become a Professional Knitter
feeds.description: I've been knitting my whole life. I started making garments for myself in my teens and then explored sewing, tailoring and millinery. I want to teach knitters about fit and flattery and turn them into fashion stars! A knitting blog about career transition, personal development and the search for fulfillment.

feeds.title: Needles and Wool
feeds.description: A blog about my love of knitting. The blog includes knitting stitch tutorials, different knitting projects, and knitting ideas.

feeds.title: Three Bags Full Yarn Store Blog
feeds.description: A place for people who love to knit. We offer beautiful yarn, fun projects and patterns, needles and other knitting accessories.

feeds.title: Prairie Knitting
feeds.description: All things knitting

feeds.title: Knitted Bliss - Knitting, crafting, and all-round awesomeness.
feeds.description: Hi I'm Julie. I love the written word, cozy knits, international travel, domestic pleasures, my quirky british husband, and my two little kids. I help knitters and crafters get inspired by sharing modified knitting projects, round ups of craft ideas and recipes, and reflections on the crafting life.
